summary: Flame in Freefall Explorer is an SI-powered web dashboard that standardizes, ranks, and interprets 746 microgravity combustion runs from NASA PSI and 28 NASA NTRS reports. Through an Engineer Workbench and a Student Physics Lab (ES/EN), it reveals critical solid-flammability gaps for Lunar Bases (≥30% O2, ≤10.2 psi), bounds partial-gravity (1/6g) risks, and exports clean CSVs for predictive fire safety modeling.
details:
1. THE PROBLEM

As humanity prepares for the Artemis Lunar Base and Pressurized Rovers, habitats will operate at ≥30% O2 and ≤10.2 psi (>40% more oxygen than Earth) to reduce astronaut spacesuit pre-breathing time. However, NASA's Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) database contains terabytes of fragmented tables with incompatible units (bar, atm, psi, mole fraction vs. % O2) and currently has zero direct lunar partial-gravity (1/6g) combustion data.

2. OUR SOLUTION & KEY SCIENTIFIC FINDINGS

We built a canonical Python/Pandas ETL pipeline and a Next.js + SI analytical platform (https://fireonflamenasa.vercel.app/) that standardizes 746 real experimental runs across 5 core PSI investigations (BASS-II, SAFFIRE-II, SAME-R, FLEX-2, ACME CFI-G) and links them to 28 peer-reviewed NASA NTRS papers:

• The Lunar Solid-Fuel Gap: Our parametric coverage map proves that 0 out of 144 solid-fuel tests in BASS-II (MSG) and SAFFIRE-II (Cygnus) exceeded 22.2% O2 due to ISS cabin constraints. Only sealed CIR chamber studies (FLEX-2 liquid droplets up to 30% O2 / 7.3 psi and ACME CFI-G gases up to 85% O2) cover the lunar oxidizing regime.

• Partial-Gravity Bounding (0g ↔ 1/6g ↔ 1g): Until future LUCI and FM2 lunar experiments arrive, our engine uses SAFFIRE-II's parallel 0g and 1g burn-length measurements on identical polymers to bound intermediate gravity fire behavior.

• Dual-Lens Architecture: (1) Engineer View provides a 100-point deterministic multi-criteria ranking, thermodynamic scatter plots, a question-aware SI Assistant, and 1-click normalized CSV export for CFD/ML modeling. (2) Student & Public View offers a real-time interactive SVG Flame Physics Simulator in Spanish & English.

3. SOCIETAL IMPACT ON EARTH (WHY THIS MATTERS TO EVERYONE)

Beyond protecting astronauts, our platform explicitly maps how each of the 5 NASA PSI datasets solves urgent problems for society on Earth today:

• Mining & Industrial Safety (SAME-R | PSI-101): Smoke particle coagulation (Rt/R0) data combined with sibling DAFT dust studies enables smart industrial detectors that distinguish harmless dust from real fire smoke in underground mines, factories, and tunnels.

• Eco-Friendly Fire Suppression for Hospitals & Data Centers (FLEX-2 | PSI-68): Droplet extinction studies inform fine-water-mist extinguishers on Earth, suppressing fires with up to 90% less water and zero toxic halon/PFAS chemicals.

• Protecting Firefighters & Public Buildings (BASS-II | PSI-25 & SAFFIRE-II | PSI-99): Ventilated polymer flammability data improves standards for firefighter protective clothing, lightweight breathing tanks, and tunnel/high-rise fire modeling.

• Cleaner Energy & STEM Education (ACME CFI-G | PSI-159): Cool-flame kinetic data helps reduce soot pollution in terrestrial engines, while our free bilingual simulator brings NASA physics to schools.

4. TOOLS & STACK

Python (Pandas, Requests), Next.js (TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Recharts), Google Gemini API (@google/genai) paired with a deterministic zero-hallucination local analytical engine. Open-source code: https://github.com/Gabriel-F-13/web

5. SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) ACKNOWLEDGMENT & TRANSPARENCY

In compliance with Space Apps SI guidelines: (a) In-App SI: Google Gemini API (gemini-2.5-flash) is used for the grounded Scientific Interpretation Assistant alongside a deterministic local analytical engine. (b) Development & Presentation: SI tools were utilized to assist with Python ETL schema normalization, bilingual (ES/EN) translation, code debugging, and presentation structuring. All scientific metrics and rankings are 100% deterministic from official NASA PSI data.
